summary: WebRender received broad rendering and architecture improvements: its GPU backend is now separated behind backend-neutral interfaces, making OpenGL, software rendering, and other backends easier to maintain and evolve. Rendering was also made more accurate and efficient through better visibility culling, device-space clipping and snapping, anti-aliasing, gradient and image fixes, and limits on oversized glyph rasterization. Developer tools gained shader hot reloading and a scene inspector, while new tests cover tricky gradients, clipping, filters, and compositor paths.
